name: Adoniram
overview: Adoniram, also known as Adoram, served as the chief tax gatherer or overseer of tribute during the reigns of King David and Solomon, illustrating the administrative structure of ancient Israel's kingdom. Scripture highlights his responsibility over the levy, managing the collection of resources vital for the kingdom's needs, including labor for projects like those in Lebanon. His role was significant yet perilous, as shown when he was stoned to death by the Israelites during King Rehoboam's reign, reflecting the tension between royal authority and the people's response to taxation.
